newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia's Tudjman sworn in for second 5-year term.
newsitem.headline: Croatia's Tudjman sworn in for second 5-year term.

text.p: President Franjo Tudjman, who led Croatia to independence from federal Yugoslavia, was sworn in for a second five-year term in office on Tuesday.

"I swear upon my honour that I will carry out my duties to the benefit of all Croatian citizens," Tudjman said at a colourful open-air ceremony, held in front of top state and church officials and foreign ambassadors in a packed central Zagreb square cordoned with police.

The 76-year-old former Yugoslav army general, rumoured to have been treated for cancer last year, looked healthy and his voice was firm, apparently confirming doctors' reports that his therapy had been successfully completed.
Tudjman crushed his opponents in the first round of June's presidential poll and immediately announced he would work to raise the living standards of impoverished Croats.

Diplomats, who often criticise Tudjman's autocratic rule, believe he holds a firm grip on Croatia's fate and could manage to bring it closer to Western Europe if he lives up to the obligations he undertook in a peace accord in late 1995.

Those commitments include handing over indicted Bosnian Croats to an international war crimes tribunal, allowing the return of all Serb war refugees and quelling nationalist Bosnian Croat opposition to a Croat-Moslem federation.
